name: silent-film
title: 1920s silent film
summary: An inked, hatched silent film projected in a picture house: a 4:3 print that flickers and weaves between velvet curtains, intertitles instead of voices, a pianist on every beat.

look.ground: a 4:3 print (1440x1080) in a rounded gate, velvet drapes lit by the screen at the sides of 16:9
look.type: intertitles as subtitles: small-caps display serif (Playfair Display SC) for titles and shouts, italic old-style serif (Old Standard TT) for narration, on black cards with deco borders
look.texture: a print pass: silver tone with 0.1-0.36 sepia, flicker, gate weave, scratches, dust, edge burn, two-octave grain
look.light: tonal painting in grey values with soft gradients; tint and damage set per section as mood (colder and harsher when things go wrong)
look.materials: ink line, washed greys and 45 degree hatching redrawn every two frames

consistency: realistic-proportion figures on a 2.5D rig, identified by a silhouette mark (a hat, a garment, a tool)

motion.feel: hand-cranked: figures and camera sampled at 16 fps, print damage every frame; deadpan faces, bodies act
moves: locked-off wide where the whole gag plays out
iris in and out, or held half-open for a look to camera
undercranked chase: speed and damage rise together
the curtain opens and closes the film

pace.text: three to five cards in a short film, a few words each, held 2.5-3.75 s; a card never explains what the picture shows

banned: dissolves within a scene or modern whip pans
a sepia filter over modern animation
the Tramp look or any real film's gags

made_with.renderer: 2D canvas with a WebGL2 ink and print pass

source: LemoLab's 1920s Silent Film style in lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar at 9eb7739; pace measured with analyze.py and events.py on its demo film "The Runaway Loaf"
